subject: Critical throughput chokepoint — Hosted API latency & p95/p99 regression
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmeapp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-support@acmeapp.com
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Spike in API p95/p99 for AcmeApp (prod-us-west) — urgent

Marcus / Monica,

We started seeing a big regression at ~08:40 PDT — p95 has moved from ~220ms to ~1.6s and p99 is now 3.2s. Error rate (5xx) jumped ~1.8% over baseline. This is impacting our search autocomplete (users see stalls). We are on the hosted API (region: prod-us-west) and didn't change workload patterns on our side.

Attached is a Grafana snapshot and a small sample request ID list. Can you confirm if this is on your side or if we're doing something wrong? This is high severity for our launch this week.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Lee
VP Product, AcmeApp

Attachments: acme-prod-grafana-screenshot.png (png), request-ids-sample.txt (text)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmeapp.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in API p95/p99 for AcmeApp (prod-us-west) — urgent

Thanks Jordan — looping Monica and Sean for immediate triage. Monica: can you pick this up? Sean: FYI / heads-up to the account team.

Quick asks:
- Monica, confirm whether this looks like a routing/queue depth buildup or model-side degradation.
- If autoscaling/replica limits are hit, propose an immediate mitigation (route to dedicated pool, increase burst capacity, or temporary batching change).

I will keep Jordan on the thread and share timeline.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmeapp.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:46:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in API p95/p99 for AcmeApp (prod-us-west) — urgent

Marcus / Jordan,

Initial triage notes (08:40–09:40 window):
- Observed sustained queue depth growth on the hosted API frontends serving AcmeApp traffic. The request queue for the primary routing bucket increased ~6x compared to baseline; batching windows expanded to ~110ms average (was ~18–25ms).
- Kernel selection telemetry shows fallback to a slower float path on a subset of hosts after a failed perf roll 3:45AM UTC (we have a partial roll that looks correlated).
- Autoscaling triggers fired but we observed a delayed lifecycle: new replicas came up but were not being routed to immediately due to shard affinity and a stale routing table entry for one AZ.
- Error rate bump appears secondary to timeouts from queue overflow, not model decoding failures.

Immediate mitigation applied at 09:38: temporarily increased per-customer concurrency cap for AcmeApp and forced routing to the warm dedicated pool (low-risk, short-burst credit). Also disabled the partial kernel roll on the affected hosts (patch rollback queued).

I'm attaching a trimmed logs bundle and a Grafana snapshot for your review. Next steps: 1) fix routing table sync, 2) complete kernel rollback, 3) tighten batching window heuristics and add a defensive cap on batch window expansion.

Attachments: replay-logs-20270214.zip (logs), acme-prod-grafana-screenshot.png (png)

— Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Site Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmeapp.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in API p95/p99 for AcmeApp (prod-us-west) — urgent

Appreciate the quick action, Monica. Marcus: I'm flagging this with the account leadership to prepare for an executive update if Acme wants it. Jordan — we'll keep you posted on timeline for the rollback and the routing sync fix.

Two quick asks from my side:
- Can we confirm impact window and number of affected requests (rough estimate)?
- Any customer-visible errors that should be surfaced to support/ops page?

I'll stand by to coordinate a short exec brief if needed.

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmeapp.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in API p95/p99 for AcmeApp (prod-us-west) — urgent

Team — thanks for the mitigation. Proposed short-term action plan for next 6 hours:
1) Complete kernel rollback on affected hosts (Monica / infra) — target 12:00 PST.
2) Enforce routing table refresh and remove stale shard affinity; add one-minute aggressive refresh on affected routing tier (Infra) — target 12:15 PST.
3) Deploy a temporary batch-window cap (max 40ms) and lower batching aggressiveness for AcmeApp routing bucket — target 12:30 PST.
4) Monitor p95/p99 and error rate for 2 hours post-change; if still elevated, plan traffic shift to dedicated pool for rest of day.

Jordan — if this plan works for you we will proceed and share post-change metrics. If you prefer a canary rollback only on the smallest footprint we can do that instead.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmeapp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, acme-support@acmeapp.com
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 13:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in API p95/p99 for AcmeApp (prod-us-west) — urgent

Marcus / Monica — thanks for the quick triage and the temporary routing change. The initial improvement looks promising in our dashboard (p95 down to ~260ms within 20 minutes). Please proceed with the rollback + routing fixes on the timeline you proposed. We will notify our on-call and pause a planned heavy traffic test later today.

One ask for post-mortem: include exact root cause (kernel roll vs routing sync) and an action item to prevent batch-window runaway from happening during partial rollouts.

Jordan
Jordan Lee
VP Product, AcmeApp
